chunks: Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi al-Hakim narrated to us, saying: He told me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Suli said: He narrated to us Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, saying: He told me my father said:

Al-Ma'mun climbed the pulpit when he pledged allegiance to Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), and said: 'O people! The pledge of allegiance to Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) has come to you. By God, if these names were recited to the deaf and dumb, they would be healed by the permission of God, the Mighty and Exalted.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.عَلِيَّ بْنَ مُوسَى الرِّضَا: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, the eighth Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Al-Ma'mun say about the names of the Imams when announcing the pledge of allegiance?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* captures the public proclamation of Imam al-Rida’s succession by Caliph Al-Ma'mun, emphasizing the spiritual potency of the Ahl al-Bayt's lineage. The reference to healing the deaf and dumb underscores the concept of *I'jaz* (infallibility/miraculousness) inherent in the Imams, suggesting that their mere names carry divine authority capable of curing spiritual and physical ailments. This event is pivotal in Shia historiography as it marks the transition of the Imamate into the political sphere under the Abbasids, albeit with underlying tensions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 40-17 Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sowli quoted on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Al-Jahm, on the authority of his father,

“When Al-Ma’mun pledged allegiance to Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.), he climbed up the pulpit and said, ‘O people! You were informed of the news of the pledge of allegiance to Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib. By God, if they read these names to the deaf and dumb, they will be healed by the permission of God the Honorable the Exalted.’”
